_comment: ASSUMPTIONS, NOT CODE FACTS. Everything in this file is either a doc figure with no on-chain source, or a modelling profile the simulation invents. Nothing here is extracted from Solidity and nothing here is covered by the drift check. Argue with this file first.

wood_total_supply.note: The production WOOD token is in neither repo. The repo holds three mutually inconsistent supply numbers (500M / 100M fixture / 1B retired). Every %-of-supply figure inherits this.

wood_effective_float_m12.note: Midpoint of the 210-250M M12 effective-float range. Every %-of-float and every binding-TVL figure inherits this.

wood_price_tokenomics_anchor.note: The buyback table's price anchor. Not a market price.

wood_price_stretch_anchors.note: No repo source at all. They exist only to show that every WOOD quantity is exactly inversely proportional to price.

certified_bound_bps.note: The protocol's own worked example for a certified tier-0/1 adapter. Real bounds are per-adapter in [1, 9999] (TierRegistry.sol:496) and NO deploy script issues any certification -- at launch everything is tier 2 at full notional.

flywheel_threshold_frac_of_float.note: The share of effective float at which required lockup is called 'binding'. Arbitrary; the report also shows 10% and 50%.

stage_profiles._comment: Invented. Fund size, cadence, proposal size, tier-2 share, approvers, gross return and win rate come from nowhere in the repo. The RATIOS the model reports (fee as % of gross, stake per $1 of coverage) are far more robust than the absolute dollars.

fee_sets._comment: mgmt_bps / perf_bps only. The splits always come from ProtocolConfig.sol via the extractor.

current.label: Current deployed defaults (2 and 20)
current.note: Both sides read from the extracted constants, so this set moves if the source moves.

she330_caps.label: #330 reading (5 and 15)
she330_caps.note: A judgement call. Two of the three #330 constants no longer exist post-audit and the perf cap was later RAISED to 3000, so '#330 targets' cannot be run literally. Read here as rate ceilings under the current two-number model.

worst_stack.label: Post-audit ceilings (5 and 30)
worst_stack.note: Every rate at its post-audit hard ceiling. This is the unambiguous SHE-18 fee-stacking case.

mgmt_capped.label: Management-capped (1 and 20)
mgmt_capped.note: Not a proposal in any ticket. It exists to test the finding that the MANAGEMENT rate, not the performance rate, is the depositor's real lever once a fund is deployed most of the year.
